US drugstore chain with 300 neighborhood pharmacies in the Midwest (~6,000 employees). Fills prescriptions (including controlled painkillers and ADHD medicines), gives flu and COVID shots, and sells over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, snacks and household goods. Most prescriptions are paid by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. No hospitals or clinics, does not make any drugs, no mail-order.

- DEA rules for pharmacies that dispense controlled substances (registration, opioids, telehealth prescribing)
- FDA rules on over-the-counter drugs, drug labeling, drug shortages and recalls that reach pharmacy shelves
- Medicare Part D and Medicaid payment and pharmacy rules (CMS)
- CDC vaccine recommendations that change what pharmacists may give
- Patient privacy (HIPAA) and pharmacy recordkeeping
- Workplace and labor rules for retail stores

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Approval, manufacturing or inspection rules aimed only at drug or device manufacturers
- Hospital, nursing-home, physician-payment or clinical-lab rules
- Research grants, clinical trials, NIH funding notices
- Banking, securities, aviation, energy, farming

[2026-23124] Proposed Rule — Environmental Protection Agency
Title: Air Plan Approval; Oregon Department of Environmental Quality; Emission Standards and Controls for Sources Emitting Gasoline Vapors
Action: Proposed rule.
Abstract: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) proposes to approve a revision to the Oregon State Implementation Plan (SIP) submitted by the Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (ODEQ) on December 17, 2025, for the Portland and Salem/Keizer, Oregon 1979 1-hour ozone maintenance areas. The proposed revision updates ODEQ's requirements in the SIP for Stages I and II vapor recovery systems at gasoline dispensing facilities including: decommissioning existing Stage II systems incompatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery systems; allowing removal from service of Stage II vapor recovery equipment compatible with onboard refueling vapor recovery; and removing the requirement for Stage II vapor recovery at new installations. The proposed revisions also include more widespread adoption of Stage I Enhanced Vapor Recovery, Stage I vapor balance, and enhanced conventional nozzles, among other changes. The EPA is proposing to find that ODEQ's demonstration to remove Stage II requirements is consistent with the Clean Air Act and the EPA's guidance.

Title: Unemployment Insurance Program National Minimum Weekly Work Search Requirements
Action: Proposed rule, request for comment.
Abstract: The U.S. Department of Labor (Department), through the Employment and Training Administration (ETA), is proposing to amend 20 CFR part 604 both to reflect a 2012 update in Federal law in which Congress, by amending section 303(a) of the Social Security Act (SSA), established a Federal work search requirement; and to establish a national minimum weekly work search requirement standard for the Federal-State unemployment compensation (UC) program. This proposed rule would mandate, among other things, that States require individuals claiming UC to complete at least five qualifying work search activities or, where applicable, meet State-adopted points-based system requirements amounting to five qualifying activities or satisfy equivalent labor force attachment criteria, each week for which UC is claimed; that individuals report their work search activities as part of their certification process prior to payment being issued; and that State law allow for certain qualifying work search activities beyond simply employer contacts. # Regulatory triage — CornerCare Pharmacy
Window 2026-11-09 → 2026-11-13 · as of 2026-11-13 · 4 items

## Critical (3)

- **Medicare Drug Price Negotiation Program and Medicare Prescription Drug Benefit Program** [Federal Register]
  - Review expected payments for affected Medicare prescriptions and update billing procedures so CornerCare can spot and resolve underpayments.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-05 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Lucia Moreno (Reimbursement) · Areas: payers
  - 91 FR 72176 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22792/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program-and-medicare-prescription-drug-benefit-program
- **Rules of Practice and Procedure for Administrative Hearings Before the Office of Administrative Law Judges** [Federal Register]
  - Set up electronic filing and designate a backup filer so CornerCare can submit paperwork on time in Department of Labor hearings.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-09 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance) · Areas: privacy-people
  - 91 FR 70790 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22761/rules-of-practice-and-procedure-for-administrative-hearings-before-the-office-of-administrative-law
- **Schedules of Controlled Substances: Placement of Oveporexton in Schedule IV** [Federal Register]
  - Check whether CornerCare plans to stock oveporexton and, if so, prepare dispensing, inventory, and recordkeeping procedures in case the proposed controls become final.
  - Deadline: 2026-12-14 (comment, FR field ✓) · Owner: Priya Raman (Pharmacy Operations) · Areas: pharmacy-ops, privacy-people
  - 91 FR 72775 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/12/2026-23075/schedules-of-controlled-substances-placement-of-oveporexton-in-schedule-iv

## High (1)

- **Rules and Regulations, Series 8** [Federal Register]
  - Update the company’s response procedures for union representation cases and complaints about unfair labor practices so store managers know whom to notify.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Sam Whitaker (Privacy & HR Compliance) · Areas: privacy-people
  - 91 FR 72419 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22891/rules-and-regulations-series-8
